method: Read-only source inspection at exact ATCLang PR head ac488bcdf2a10be2c9ecc22fc1555444f5de0ccb; normative registry and all listed Rust frontend/runtime/test files were re-fetched by exact commit and blob SHA. GitHub Actions evidence is recorded separately. Workflow success does not classify individual language requirements as VERIFIED; no per-item semantic equivalence has been established. Registry rows remain UNRESOLVED / NOT_RUN unless individually proven.

semantic_observations.finding: The canonical Rust lexer explicitly emits a narrow Token enum; recognized keyword spellings include let, const, return, fn, if, else, while, contract, state, function, capability, policy, require. Other words fall through to Ident.
semantic_observations.impact: Registry keyword presence does not establish parser or runtime semantics; each keyword needs grammar/use-site mapping and positive/negative behavior tests.

semantic_observations.finding: The canonical parser is a recursive-descent subset centered on let/const, function declarations, brace-delimited blocks, if/else, while, return, and arithmetic/comparison/call expressions.
semantic_observations.impact: Registry productions require semantic reconciliation against actual parser entry points; a method-name match is insufficient.

semantic_observations.finding: The AST uses a limited Expr/Stmt model, including integer literals, identifiers, unary/binary operations, calls, let, function, return, expression, if, and while.
semantic_observations.impact: No AST variant name match is not by itself proof of missing support; equivalent representation or intentionally unsupported syntax must be checked.

semantic_observations.finding: native.rs implements a separate native contract frontend with contract/state/function parsing and semantic validation, including rejection tests for malformed or unknown directives/types/decorators.
semantic_observations.impact: Native contract syntax must not be mistaken for general language grammar coverage; identify exact entry points and delegation boundaries.

semantic_observations.finding: lower.rs lowers the restricted AST to bytecode and contains end-to-end tests for arithmetic, branching, loops, calls, and fail-closed handling of unsupported operators.
semantic_observations.impact: Passing source presence is not test execution; current report records no test run.

semantic_observations.finding: value.rs defines an explicit ABI type/value model; textual type-name matches need conversion, validation, and runtime-use evidence.
semantic_observations.impact: Type spelling alone does not prove type-system conformance.

semantic_observations.finding: The exact PR head adds checked decimal overflow handling and checked 0x/0o/0b integer parsing in the canonical Rust lexer, with positive and malformed-input regression tests in source.
semantic_observations.impact: This is a bounded lexer improvement only. The Rust lexer emits Token::Int(u64), whereas the normative registry distinguishes INT, HEX_INT, OCTAL_INT, and BIN_INT. Equivalence or intentional normalization is not yet specified/proven; these entries remain UNRESOLVED.

required_next_actions: Classify each of the 332 rows MAPPED, EXCLUDED, or UNRESOLVED only after inspecting normative definition and actual lexer/parser/AST/lowering/runtime call path; include exact file/blob/symbol/test evidence.
Resolve the normative token-category question for INT versus HEX_INT/OCTAL_INT/BIN_INT and prove any proposed normalization with semantics and tests.
Separate unsupported normative requirements from equivalent representations, native-only contracts, delegated behavior, and explicitly excluded scope.
Inspect and repair the failed independent governance/security audit, Markdown lint, and code-quality workflow findings; capture full step logs and numeric exit codes.
Run relevant workflows again against the exact source SHA after fixes; preserve run/job/step/artifact hashes.
Keep all unproven registry entries UNRESOLVED / NOT_RUN and retain RESIDUAL/BLOCKED until item-level acceptance criteria pass.
